cohort: 12,915 singleton SGA neonates born at the Soroka University Medical Center between 1998-2013
finding: SGA pregnancies complicated with iSUA are at higher risk for adverse pregnancy and perinatal outcomes compared to SGA pregnancies without iSUA.
mod_finding: Pregnancies complicated by isolated single umbilical artery among small for gestational age neonates were associated with higher rates of cesarean deliveries.
birth_weight: Lower in the iSUA group (1988.0 ± 697g vs. 2388.3 ± 481g, p < 0.001)
